operations_plan.summary: Create three separated, longitudinal capsule-shaped through-cut lightening openings in the central tapered arm. Use conservative, taper-adjusted sizes because the request does not specify the cutout count, shape, dimensions, spacing, depth, or minimum wall thickness. Preserve the pivot clevis, hook, and complete exterior silhouette.

steps.description: Identify the editable span of the central tapered load-carrying arm (section_2, feature_2_1) between the left pivot clevis and the right hook. Retrieve the actual X extents and the upper and lower arm boundaries from planar faces 5 and 11. Treat section_1 and section_3 as protected exclusion regions. Establish end-clearance limits inside the arm, nominally restricting cutouts to approximately x=-52 mm through x=35 mm so that material remains uninterrupted next to the clevis slot end near x=-60.75 mm and ahead of the hook root.

Create or select the global XZ center plane at y=0 as the sketch plane. This plane lies midway between the positive-Y and negative-Y sides of the symmetric arm and permits a cut normal to the plane, along the Y direction, through the complete arm thickness. Project or intersect faces 5 and 11 into the sketch to obtain the local upper and lower tapered boundaries; also project the clevis-side and hook-side transition limits as construction references.

Construct a longitudinal arm centerline in the XZ sketch by taking the midpoint between the projected upper face 5 and lower face 11 boundaries. If the two boundaries are symmetric, use the nominal constant elevation z=7.5 mm indicated by the pivot-bore axis; otherwise use a construction spline or line through the local boundary midpoints. Constrain every lightening opening symmetrically about this centerline so that equal upper and lower load-carrying rails remain.

Draw three nonintersecting closed capsule-slot profiles with their major axes parallel to the X direction and their centers on the arm centerline. Use nominal profiles: slot A from x=-52 mm to x=-30 mm with 5.0 mm width and 2.5 mm end radii; slot B from x=-23 mm to x=0 mm with 4.5 mm width and 2.25 mm end radii; and slot C from x=8 mm to x=35 mm with 3.5 mm width and 1.75 mm end radii. Fully constrain each profile using two tangent longitudinal lines and semicircular ends. These values are design assumptions resolving the unspecified number and size of cutouts; reduce a slot width or shorten its ends if the measured tapered envelope cannot maintain the required margins.

Constrain the three profiles to remain completely internal to the projected arm envelope. Maintain at least 2.0 mm of uninterrupted material between every slot and each projected upper or lower boundary, at least 6.0 mm between adjacent slot ends, and at least 8.0 mm between the outermost slots and either functional end transition. If any nominal profile violates these rules because of the actual local taper, reduce that profile uniformly about its centerline rather than moving or modifying the external arm boundary.

Perform one symmetric through-all extruded cut from the three closed sketch regions in both +Y and -Y directions. Set the termination to Through All or Through All Both so that each opening completely intersects the positive-Y and negative-Y longitudinal side skins, faces 16 and 9, despite their taper. Boolean-subtract the resulting three cutting tools from solid 0 while retaining a single connected solid.

Regenerate and validate the result. Confirm that three separate through-openings exist only in section_2; that no opening intersects the clevis lugs, slot, pivot-bore faces 0 and 1, hook throat faces 7 and 8, or hook heel/catch faces 10, 13, and 17; and that the outer tapered faces 5 and 11 remain unchanged. Verify that solid 0 remains one watertight connected body, all slot ends are rounded, and continuous upper, lower, and inter-slot load paths remain around the openings.
